title: Etale local invariance at a point with algebraically closed residue field
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $C$ be a locally finite type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $e:D\to C$ be etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. For $y\in D$ with $x=e(y)$, if either residue field $\kappa(x)$ or $\kappa(y)$ [def-weil-residue-field] is isomorphic to $k$ as a $k$-algebra (that is, the field map $k\to\kappa(x)$, resp. $k\to\kappa(y)$, induced by the structure morphism $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, resp. $D\to C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, is an isomorphism), then $x$ and $y$ are closed points [def-weil-closed-points], the induced residue-field map $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(y)$ is an isomorphism, and the induced map on maximal-ideal-adic completed local rings $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{C,x}\to\widehat{\mathcal O}_{D,y}$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] is an isomorphism.

source.place: Morphisms Tag 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field) part (2): the residue extension kappa(y)/kappa(x) of an etale morphism is finite separable, hence trivial over kappa(x)=k algebraically closed; Morphisms Tag 01TE (lemma-algebraic-residue-field-extension-closed-point-fibre) (2): a point with residue field algebraic over k is closed in a k-scheme; More on Algebra Tag 0AGX (lemma-flat-unramified), or Etale Morphisms Tag 039M (lemma-characterize-etale-completions) with the remark following it: the flat local map O_{C,x} -> O_{D,y} with m_x O_{D,y}=m_y and trivial residue extension induces an isomorphism of completions. This is the argument of the proof of Curves Tag 0C57.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_{C,x}$, $B=\mathcal O_{D,y}$ and let $\varphi:A\to B$ be the actual stalk map of $e$. By [def-weil-etale-morphism], $e$ is flat and unramified; by [def-weil-unramified-morphism] it is locally of finite type. By [def-weil-flat-morphism], $\varphi$ is a flat local homomorphism. Thus neither flatness nor locality is being inferred from a merely abstract isomorphism of rings.

Apply implication (i)$\Rightarrow$(ii) of [lem-trf-unramified-maximal-ideal-residue-criterion] to $e$ at $y$, using the whole source $D$ as the unramified neighbourhood. Its locally-finite-type hypothesis holds by Step 1. It gives $\mathfrak m_A B=\mathfrak m_B$ for $\varphi$, and says that the actual induced map $\alpha:\kappa(x)\to\kappa(y)$ is a finite separable algebraic field extension.

Write $i:k\to\kappa(x)$ and $j:k\to\kappa(y)$ for the structural field maps. Functoriality of the maps induced on stalk quotients in [def-weil-residue-field] gives $j=\alpha i$. If $i$ is an isomorphism, every element of $\kappa(y)$ is algebraic over the image of $j$, by Step 2. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-over-algebraically-closed-subfield] to each element: every element lies in $j(k)$. Thus $j$ is surjective, and $\alpha$ is surjective as well. Field maps are injective, so both are isomorphisms. If instead $j$ is an isomorphism, then for $a\in\kappa(x)$ take $c\in k$ with $j(c)=\alpha(a)$; injectivity of $\alpha$ gives $i(c)=a$. Thus $i$ is an isomorphism, and $\alpha=j i^{-1}$ is one too. In both cases the structural maps $i,j$, as well as $\alpha$, are isomorphisms, not just abstract field identifications.

source.place: Tags 09GQ (definition-algebraically-closed) and 09GR (lemma-algebraically-closed); elementary factorization for the second case

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-residue-point-closed-in-fibre] to the structural morphism $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. It is locally of finite type by hypothesis, and Step 3 says that its residue-field extension at $x$ has degree one. Hence $x$ is closed in the scheme-theoretic fibre over the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}k$. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum] this base has one point; by [def-pc-scheme-fibre] that fibre is homeomorphic to all of $C$. Consequently $x$ is closed in $C$.

source.place: Tag 01TE (lemma-algebraic-residue-field-extension-closed-point-fibre), applied to C over Spec k

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-residue-point-closed-in-fibre] to $e$, which is locally of finite type by Step 1. The residue extension at $y$ is finite by Step 2 (indeed degree one by Step 3). Thus $y$ is closed in $D_x$. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre], $D_x$ is homeomorphic to the subspace $e^{-1}(\{x\})$. This subspace is closed in $D$, because $x$ is closed by Step 4 and $e$ is continuous. A subset closed in a closed subspace is closed in the ambient space, so $y$ is closed in $D$.

source.place: Tag 01TE, closedness in the fibre and elementary topology in its proof

proof.text: The field $k$ is Noetherian: its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$, both finitely generated. Hence $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Apply [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] first to $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, then to $e:D\to C$, using its local finite type from Step 1. Both $C$ and $D$ are locally Noetherian. Choose, from the affine covers in [pqf-def-locnoeth], an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $x$ and one $V=\operatorname{Spec}S$ of $y$ with $R,S$ Noetherian. By clause (c) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], the germ maps $R\to A$ and $S\to B$ are localizations at the corresponding primes. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] to these two maps. Thus $A$ and $B$ are Noetherian local rings, as required for the completion theorem. No global quasi-compactness is needed.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-completion-iso] to the actual map $\varphi:A\to B$. Its hypotheses are verified separately: Noetherian local rings by Step 6, flatness and locality by Step 1, $\mathfrak m_AB=\mathfrak m_B$ by Step 2, and an isomorphism on residue fields by Step 3. Its conclusion is that $\varphi^\wedge:A^\wedge\to B^\wedge$ is an isomorphism. The cited statement specifies this very map on compatible residue classes by $(a_n\bmod\mathfrak m_A^n)_n\mapsto(\varphi(a_n)\bmod\mathfrak m_B^n)_n$, so it is exactly the induced completed-local-ring map in the item. Together with Steps 3--5 this proves all the required clauses.

Step 1 only unpacks definitions: étale gives flat and unramified, unramified includes locally finite type, and the flat-morphism definition makes the stalk map a flat local homomorphism. Step 2 applies the 02GF criterion with V=D. Step 3 handles both cases using the structural maps (j = alpha i), and the hypothesis of the algebraic-over-algebraically-closed leaf holds. Steps 4 and 5 use 01TE, the one-point base Spec k and the homeomorphism of the fibre onto the preimage. Step 6 gets Noetherian stalks from local Noetherianity (01T6, used twice) and localization (00FN). Step 7 checks all four hypotheses of lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-completion-iso, whose completed map is exactly the induced map in the item. lean.statement: theorem etale_completedLocalRing_iso {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {C D : Scheme.{u}} (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (e : D ⟶ C) [Etale e] (y : D) (hres : Function.Bijective (((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop ≫ C.Γevaluation (e y)).hom) ∨ Function.Bijective (((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ (e ≫ f).appTop ≫ D.Γevaluation y).hom)) : e y ∈ closedPoints C ∧ y ∈ closedPoints D ∧ IsIso (e.residueFieldMap y) ∧ ∃ (ehat : AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (C.presheaf.stalk (e y))) (C.presheaf.stalk (e y)) →+* AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (D.presheaf.stalk y)) (D.presheaf.stalk y)), (∀ (n : ℕ) (z : AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (C.presheaf.stalk (e y))) (C.presheaf.stalk (e y))) (a : C.presheaf.stalk (e y)), AdicCompletion.evalₐ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (C.presheaf.stalk (e y))) n z = Ideal.Quotient.mk (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (C.presheaf.stalk (e y)) ^ n) a → AdicCompletion.evalₐ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (D.presheaf.stalk y)) n (ehat z) = Ideal.Quotient.mk (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (D.presheaf.stalk y) ^ n) ((e.stalkMap y).hom a)) ∧ Function.Bijective ehat
